messages.content: 你能先找出法國在1800年至1900年間與「戰爭」和「經濟」有關的重要歷史事件嗎？之後，你可以告訴我藝術家「奧古斯特·羅丹」創作的雕塑「沉思者」的現在市場價值嗎？最後，我也想知道1882年創作的雕塑「吻」的市場價值，也是由「奧古斯特·羅丹」創作的。

function.name: get_sculpture_value
function.description: Retrieve the current market value of a particular sculpture by a specific artist. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

artist.description: The name of the artist who created the sculpture.

year.description: The year the sculpture was created. This is optional and is not required for all sculptures. Default is the current year.

function.name: history_get_key_events
function.description: Retrieve key historical events within a specific period for a certain country. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

country.description: The name of the country for which history is queried.

start_year.description: Start year of the period for which history is queried.

end_year.description: End year of the period for which history is queried.

event_type.description: Types of event. If none is provided, default that all types will be considered.

message.reasoning:
The user wants:

1) Find important historical events in France between 1800-1900 related to War and Economy.

We need to use the function `history_get_key_events` with parameters:
country="France", start_year=1800, end_year=1900, event_type=["War","Economy"] (or maybe separate calls? But we can pass array). According to definition, event_type may accept an array or single type; but it's typed as `"War" | "Revolutions" | "Diplomacy" | "Economy"[]. Wait the typing shows union plus array? It says event_type?: "War" | "Revolutions" | "Diplomacy" | "Economy"[], so it expects either one of those strings OR an array of them. So passing ["War","Economy"] should work.

So call function.

Then ask about sculpture values:

Use get_sculpture_value twice:

First: sculpture="Le Penseur" (but Chinese translation "沉思者"? Might be Le Penseur), artist="Auguste Rodin". Year unspecified -> defaults to current year. We want current market value.

Second: sculpture="L'Embrassement" ("吻") from 1882. Provide year=1882.

Thus two function calls.

We'll produce output after retrieving results.

Let's do first function call.
